about.title: Selma Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A fall can happen in seconds — a wet floor near Highland Avenue, a cracked walkway off Golden State Boulevard, a poorly lit stairwell in an apartment complex — but the aftermath often lingers for months. In Selma, these cases turn on one central question: did the property owner or manager know, or should they have reasonably known, about the hazard before you got hurt? California law doesn't automatically hold an owner responsible just because someone fell on their property. Notice matters, and so does timing. Surveillance footage from a grocery store or business often gets erased within days or weeks unless someone requests it quickly. We're here to help Selma residents understand premises liability law, gather evidence, evaluate fault, and pursue a claim on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Fall in Selma

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. We can help identify prior complaints, maintenance logs, or inspection records that establish that notice.

items.title: Evidence Disappears Fast
items.desc: Surveillance video and incident reports at Selma businesses are often overwritten or discarded within a short window. Acting quickly to request preservation of footage can make a real difference in what evidence survives.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Recovery
items.desc: Even if a property owner argues you weren't watching where you stepped, California's pure comparative fault rule means you may still recover a share of damages proportional to the other party's responsibility.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Selma?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit, though claims against a public entity — like a city-owned sidewalk or building — often require much faster notice, sometimes within six months. Because Selma has both private businesses and public property along its main corridors, it's worth confirming the property type early. Missing a deadline can end a claim before it starts.

items.question: What if I fell at a store on Golden State Boulevard or Floral Avenue and didn't report it right away?
items.answer: Not reporting immediately doesn't automatically bar a claim, but it can make proving what happened harder. Try to write down details as soon as you remember them — date, time, lighting, weather, what you saw on the floor — and request any available surveillance footage as soon as possible. We can help send preservation letters to businesses along Selma's busier retail corridors.

items.question: Will it matter if I was partly at fault for not seeing the hazard?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by your percentage of responsibility rather than eliminated entirely. So even if a property owner claims you should have noticed the spill or uneven pavement, you may still have a valid claim worth exploring with us.
